> What do your instructions say about creating tasks and managing their life cycle?

## Creating tasks
- **Every ask gets a task on my session's page**, made with the `item` tool: `tasks: {add: {title, description}}`. The description holds your words, polished.
- **A note** is a task titled `Note: <what>`.
- **A planned child session** is `tasks: {add: {type: "Session", ...}}`. A mastermind I spawn links itself under my session, with its cost.
- **A real build or fix** nests under the Prompt for that thought, so the chat shows it under the right bubble.
- **A task about a page** goes in that page's module home, `<page>tasks/`. Then I hand it to the page's manager with `ask_manager`, and write a feed line with `dir_log`.

## Managing the life cycle
- **Refine, don't duplicate.** When you revise an ask, I change the existing task's title and description rather than adding a second one.
- **State changes use verbs on the task id:** `start`, `wait`, `complete`, `finish`, `pause`, `resume`, `stop`, `reject`, and `approve` or `improve` for a review verdict. I use them when work starts, finishes or is dropped.
- **Read it back** with `item({path})` and no delta.
- **Owner-only:** `complete` on a Question is yours. Marking it read is never mine.

## Who does the work
- **Small page changes** go to `quick_fix`.
- **File-changing work** goes to a `mastermind` in a worktree. It is reviewed and lands through `node Server/merge.mjs`.
- **After handing off,** I check on it and verify the result myself.
- **Statements are not requests.** I only spawn work on a clear ask.

## Where I fell short today
I made the task late, after I had already messaged the other agents. You asked for tasks to define the work, assign it and track it to done, and the instructions say the same. I should have made the task first.

The instructions also have a few things I haven't done yet for this ask. I haven't written the `dir_log` decision line, and I haven't named this session with `session_summary`, which failed twice. Do you want me to do those now?

> What are the life cycle verbs?

I know the names from the `item` tool's method list on a session or task. I haven't read the code, so the meanings are my reading of the names, not confirmed.

## Running
- **`start`:** begin the task. I called this on the session-dropdown task.
- **`pause` / `resume`:** hold it and pick it back up.
- **`stop`:** end it without finishing.
- **`wait`:** park it waiting on someone. The call takes a target, e.g. `{"wait":{"on":"owner"}}`.

## Finishing
- **`complete` / `finish`:** mark it done. I believe `complete` is the owner's call on a Question, and I don't use it there.
- **`reopened`:** it exists as a method, probably for bringing a finished task back.

## Review
- **`verdict`:** record a review result.
- **`approve` / `improve` / `reject`:** the three outcomes of a review.

## Checking
- **`check` / `can`:** test what state a task is in, or whether a verb is allowed.
- **`unproven`:** probably lists work without proof it works.

I can read the code in `core/` for the `Task` class and give you the exact states and which verb moves between them. Do you want me to?

> Can the PWA keep the microphone going when I switch apps, like a phone call?

**Short answer: not reliably, as a plain PWA.**

- **Android Chrome and PWAs:** the browser suspends microphone capture when the page goes to the background or the screen locks. Installing as a PWA doesn't change that. - **Partial tricks:** a Media Session notification and a silent audio track can sometimes keep a page alive. They are unreliable, differ by phone, and I wouldn't depend on them for dictation.
- **What does work:** a thin native Android wrapper whose only job is the foreground microphone service and streaming audio to this site's server. The Claude app does this natively.

chat.text:
> What APIs would let a PWA keep the microphone going in the background?

## In a PWA (partial, unreliable)
- **Media Session API:** shows a playback-style notification with controls. It can keep a page that is playing audio from being frozen, but it doesn't keep microphone capture alive.
- **Web Locks and Wake Lock:** Screen Wake Lock keeps the screen on, which works only while the app stays in the foreground. It does nothing once you switch apps.
- **Background Sync / service workers:** these can't hold a microphone. A service worker has no `getUserMedia`.
- **Picture-in-Picture:** a document PiP window sometimes keeps a page "visible" enough to keep running. Chrome desktop supports it, and it's flaky on Android.

None of these gives you the call-style notification and a guaranteed live microphone.

## Native Android (reliable)
- **Foreground service** with `foregroundServiceType="microphone"`, which shows the ongoing-call-style notification.
- **`AudioRecord`** to capture the audio inside that service.
- **`ConnectionService` / self-managed call** (Telecom API), if you want it to behave like a real call, including audio focus and Bluetooth routing.

You'd stream the audio to this site's server over a WebSocket.

## Practical route
A thin Capacitor or Kotlin app can show this same site in a WebView and add a small foreground-service plugin for the microphone. The site stays the same, and only that plugin is native.

I can write this up as a task under that module if you want it filed.

## The 17929 to 17930 jump

> What's the significance of the 29 to 30 jump?

There isn't any. The ids are milliseconds since 1970, and the digits just roll over. The fifth digit changes every 10⁸ ms, about **27.8 hours**. The jump from `17929…` to `17930…` happened at 02:33 Central on Oct 26, which is roughly when you went to bed. It's a coincidence of the decimal digits.

That's another reason the raw ids are a bad label. A Prompt should show its title, or the time it was said, instead.

It covers about 27.8 hours (100,000 seconds), and it isn't a benchmark. It is just where a ten-million-count roll falls in a clock counted in milliseconds. Prompts made within the same 27.8-hour span share the first five digits, which is why they all look alike. Other rolls of the same clock are 1 second per 1,000 and 1 hour per 3.6 million.

- Cleaning: keep as close to verbatim as possible; fast seat fixes capitalisation and punctuation, turns spoken 'slash'/'dot' into symbols, adds mention references (links) and markdown (e.g. inline code).
- Each Whisper sentence (ends with . or ?) is relayed at once to both fast and smart seats; smart seat wakes and replies on a pause or a question.
- Raw Whisper shows light gray while moving and turns solid black when finalized; that colour change is reserved only for finalization.
- No debug noise in the chat; only subtle indicators.

add.description: Each sentence the owner says is its own timestamped Prompt: raw = exactly what Whisper sent, text = the cleaned version beside it. No paragraphs list. add.title: Shape: a Prompt line is just id, raw, text
add.description: {"tasks":{"add":{"type":"Prompt","id":"p-<ms>","raw":["what Whisper sent"]}}} then cleaning is {"p-<ms>":{"text":"Cleaned."}} and a reply is {"p-<ms>":{"replies":{"add":{...}}}}. Every field already exists on Prompt; the data structure does not change.

add.title: Old logs and V1 keep replaying
add.description: Prompt already reads raw and text with paragraphs optional: no paragraphs means cleaned falls back to the raw words, and sentences are split from them. So B writes a subset of today's shape. Old multi-paragraph Prompts replay unchanged and draw as one card each; only new Prompts are one sentence. V1 keeps reading the {chat} lines, which are still written. Proof before any merge: the V1 in-place test and the session readers on a copy of a real log.

add.title: Gains
add.description: Lighter and simpler: no Paragraphs list, no append/replace verbs, no open-Prompt timer (assign_prompt and prompt_close_ms go away). Time order is free. Cleaning is one plain set. A Whisper guess, if ever kept, is a plain set of text.

add.title: Costs
add.description: 1) Many more tasks (about 80 Prompts for one long dictation) in the session tally and the completion roll-up: a Prompt with no ask under it stays open, so the tally needs a rule (a sentence with no ask counts as settled). 2) Parts, uncovered and Prompt.trace work per Prompt, so a thought spanning sentences needs its parts on the Group card, not the Prompt. 3) Until the smart seat groups them, the chat is a flat list of sentence cards, so grouping stops being optional. 4) Questions and asks anchor to a sentence by Prompt id instead of paragraph and sentence id.

add.title: Recommendation, owner can overturn
add.description: Try B for new Prompts only, behind the same V3 view, once step 1 and 2 of Option A (replies show, one Question card) have landed. The Group overlay and the V1-unchanged proof are the same in both options, so choosing B later costs nothing now.
